I've seen some very expensive portable solar power systems. The system size is based on what your needs are. But if you're trying to power a refrigerator in an emergency situation I believe you are allocating resources (time, money, materials) incorrectly. Here's my solution to a portable power source. Both from Amazon. (Sorry, Voat does not allow links to Amazon.)

My needs: Source of power for LED flashlights mainly. I don't need them in an emergency situation, they are just small, convenient and easy to keep charged.

  • The solar panels integrated into a battery bank are far too small to charge them up well. Don't bother with them.
  • 20000mah powerbank. There are several brands of these. One by iMuto for $30. There are several other brands on Amazon.
  • Solar charger by Anker. Anker is a quality product and they make lots of electronics. When in doubt, get Anker products from Amazon. Anker 21w solar charger. $60usd.

Notes about powerbanks and solar chargers.

  • The solar panels integrated into some powerbanks are far too small to be of much use. Don't bother with them.
  • Because of the way powerbanks are rated, the actual output of the powerbank will only be 80% of the rated output, and that's being conservative because most makers use Chinese parts which are not super efficient. So you should get 16000mah from a 20000mah powerbank. This is an industry standard. There are plenty of Youtube videos explaining how to get the real capacity of a powerbank. If you are getting less than 80% of the rated capacity, you have a bad powerbank, or a really inefficient voltage convertor.
  • Due to how solar chargers are rated (and all solar panels) the actual output, on a perfectly sunny day, with the solar panel in the perfect position so the sun's rays hit the panel at 90 degree angle, the output is 80% of the rated output. So a 21w solar panel actually only generates 16.8w on a perfect day with maximum sun. This is why you should buy a bigger solar panel than you need. Output is even worse on cloudy days and if the panel is at the wrong angle with the sun.
